```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 3.6)
```

Downloading nighttime lights is a solved problem. Turning them into a panel
you can defend in a referee report is not. Three problems come up in almost
every applied project, and they matter most at high latitude:

1. **Sensor continuity.** NOAA ended Suomi NPP data delivery on 2 November
   2026. Any VIIRS series that runs past October 2026 has to switch to NOAA-20,
   and the switch must not show up as a fake shock.
2. **Coverage.** Around the June solstice VIIRS cannot observe northern
   Kazakhstan at night. A monthly sum over the pixels that remain mixes
   "dark" with "unobserved".
3. **Units.** Boundaries change (Kazakhstan created Abai, Zhetysu and Ulytau
   in 2022), and treatment is often defined by distance to a site.

`ntlpanel` makes each of these an explicit, recorded step. This vignette runs
the whole workflow on the **synthetic** data shipped with the package, which
mimics these problems, and ends with the code for a real Kazakhstan panel.

```{r}
library(ntlpanel)
ex <- ntl_example()
```

## 1. Index the files

`ntl_sources()` lists the supported products. Black Marble products can be
downloaded with `ntl_fetch()`. Other products, such as these EOG-format
monthly composites, are indexed with `ntl_files()`.

```{r}
ntl_sources()[, c("id", "frequency", "backend")]
m <- ntl_files(ex$dir, "eog_vnl_monthly")
m
table(m$series)
```

Each EOG file is paired with its cloud-free coverage (`cf_cvg`) file. The
two platforms, Suomi NPP (`npp`) and NOAA-20 (`j01`), become separate series.

## 2. Extract with coverage diagnostics

`ntl_extract()` reads one period at a time, masks pixels and computes exact
zonal statistics. `min_obs = 2` drops pixels with fewer than two
cloud-free observations. Pixels with zero observations are always treated as
unobserved, even though EOG files store 0 radiance there.

```{r}
long <- ntl_extract(m, ex$units_old, id_col = "district", min_obs = 2, quiet = TRUE)
long[long$period == as.Date("2022-06-01"),
     c("district", "series", "ntl_sum", "share_valid", "share_masked", "mean_obs")]
```

In June the three northern districts have `share_valid = 0` and
`ntl_sum = NA`, not 0. The southern districts are fully observed.

## 3. Splice the two satellites

The NOAA-20 series reads about 8% brighter. `ntl_splice()` estimates the
relationship on overlap months, rescales Suomi NPP to the NOAA-20 level and
switches to NOAA-20 from its first month.

```{r}
sp <- ntl_splice(long, from = "eog_vnl_monthly_npp", to = "eog_vnl_monthly_j01")
ntl_splice_report(sp)[, c("district", "n_overlap", "level_shift_pct", "cor", "ratio_cv", "b")]
```

`level_shift_pct` is the gap between sensors. A large or unit-specific shift,
or a high `ratio_cv` (an unstable month-to-month ratio), means the splice
needs care. With `by_month = TRUE` the calibration is estimated separately
for each calendar month.

```{r, fig.alt = "Raw and spliced series for district D5"}
d5 <- long[long$district == "D5", ]
s5 <- sp[sp$district == "D5", ]
plot(s5$period, s5$ntl_sum, type = "l", lwd = 2, xlab = "", ylab = "Sum of lights",
     main = "District D5: raw sensors and spliced series")
for (s in unique(d5$series)) {
  z <- d5[d5$series == s, ]
  lines(z$period, z$ntl_sum, lty = 2, col = if (grepl("j01", s)) "firebrick" else "steelblue")
}
legend("topleft", c("spliced", "Suomi NPP (raw)", "NOAA-20 (raw)"), lty = c(1, 2, 2),
       col = c("black", "steelblue", "firebrick"), bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
```

## 4. Build the panel and decide what to do with gaps

`ntl_panel()` balances the panel and adds time indices and a transformed
outcome. `min_share_valid` turns poorly observed cells into explicit
missing values.

```{r}
p <- ntl_panel(sp, min_share_valid = 0.5, transform = "log1p")
p
```

`ntl_gapfill()` applies one rule and records it. It also flags the
unit-months at risk of stray-light gaps.

```{r}
p_int <- ntl_gapfill(p, rule = "interp", max_gap = 2,
                     units = ex$units_old, lat_threshold = 49)
attr(p_int, "gap_report")
table(imputed = p_int$imputed, risk = p_int$stray_light_risk)
```

All 18 missing northern summer cells are bridged by interpolation and
flagged as imputed, so results can be checked with and without them. The
seasonal rule cannot fill them, because June and July are never observed in
the north. That is the honest answer. The alternatives are to interpolate
(as above), to drop those months, or to work with annual data.

## 5. Add treatment exposure

Two synthetic sites switch on in June 2022 and March 2023.
`ntl_exposure()` gives each district its distance ring and the first
treatment date within the largest ring. That date is the cohort variable
for staggered difference-in-differences estimators.

```{r}
e <- ntl_exposure(ex$units_old, ex$sites, rings = c(50, 100, 200),
                  id_col = "district", site_id_col = "site", site_time_col = "start")
e
```

```{r}
panel <- merge(as.data.frame(p_int), e[, c("district", "within_50km", "first_treat")],
               by = "district")
panel$post <- !is.na(panel$first_treat) & panel$period >= panel$first_treat
panel$treated <- panel$post & panel$within_50km
fit <- lm(ntl ~ treated + factor(district) + factor(period), data = panel,
          subset = !imputed)
coef(summary(fit))["treatedTRUE", ]
```

With fixest you would write
`feols(ntl ~ treated | district + t, data = panel[!panel$imputed, ], cluster = ~district)`.
For staggered adoption, pass `first_treat` to `did::att_gt()`.

## 6. Move official statistics across boundary vintages

Nighttime lights never need a crosswalk: you re-extract them with the new
boundaries. Official statistics often exist in only one vintage, though.
`ntl_crosswalk()` builds weights (area, or lights as below) and
`ntl_apply_crosswalk()` applies them.

```{r}
lights <- ntl_read(m, period = "2022-01", series = "eog_vnl_monthly_npp")$value
xw <- ntl_crosswalk(ex$units_old, ex$units_new, "district", "district_new",
                    weight_raster = lights)
xw
stats <- data.frame(district = ex$units_old$district, year = 2022,
                    employment = c(120, 80, 60, 150, 90, 40),
                    unemployment_rate = c(5, 7, 6, 4, 8, 9))
ntl_apply_crosswalk(stats, xw, "district", vars = c("employment", "unemployment_rate"),
                    type = c("extensive", "intensive"), by = "year")
```

## 7. The real thing: Kazakhstan with Black Marble

The code below is not run when the vignette is built. It needs a NASA
Earthdata token in `EARTHDATA_TOKEN` and region boundaries in the 2022
vintage (17 regions plus the cities of national significance). A monthly
Black Marble tile is roughly 50-130 MB and Kazakhstan needs 10 of them, so
the loop downloads one year at a time and clears the cache after each year.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(sf)
regions <- st_read("kz_adm1_2022.gpkg")        # your boundaries, column "region"
ntl_tiles(regions)                             # 10 tiles: h22-h26, v03-v04

extract_year <- function(product, year) {
  m <- ntl_fetch(product, aoi = regions, start = paste0(year, "-01"),
                 end = paste0(year, "-12"))
  out <- ntl_extract(m, regions, id_col = "region", quality_max = 1)
  ntl_cache_clear(m)
  out
}
snpp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(2014:2026, function(y) extract_year("VNP46A3", y)))
j01  <- do.call(rbind, lapply(2018:2026, function(y) extract_year("VJ146A3", y)))

sp <- ntl_splice(rbind(snpp, j01), from = "VNP46A3", to = "VJ146A3",
                 by_month = TRUE, min_share_valid = 0.8)
ntl_splice_report(sp)

p <- ntl_panel(sp, min_share_valid = 0.6)
p <- ntl_gapfill(p, rule = "interp", max_gap = 2, units = regions, lat_threshold = 45)
```

Before you commit to a long monthly series, run
`system.file("scripts", "validate_splice_kz.R", package = "ntlpanel")`. It
checks tile orientation and whether the Suomi NPP to NOAA-20 shift is
stable across Kazakhstan's regions and seasons.
